_comment: Guest functions replaced by native code (src/game/overrides). The original is still compiled as f_<addr> and callable from the override.

overrides.why: list_cursor_update: for the card lists only (Card Menu, Deck Edit card selection, Fusion Shop), Left/Right also page like L2/R2 while the original runs (src/game/overrides/list_paging.cpp)
pad_update: on the title (light ball, Press Start Button) any button also counts as Start (src/game/overrides/title_input.cpp)
task switch: saves context and jumps into another task's stack
task switch: sleep n frames (yield n times)
task switch: return address of every task entry; unlinks and switches away
file API: cache a directory for relative paths; served natively, no CD reads
file API: open X:\DIR\NAME.EXT via the archive tables; served natively
file API: close a handle
file API: read into RAM; native, instant (the original polls CdReadSync)
play movie N (0 opening, 1 credits, 2 BANDAI logo): native MPEG-1 from movie/movie<N>.mpg when present, else the CD stream
city_msg_build: English city lines (grafted US scripts, catalog hits) kept host-side; the original drops ASCII and has no length check (src/game/overrides/city_text.cpp)
city_msg_reveal: typewriter for those English lines, drawn through the text renderer

tutorial_msg_show: English tutorial lines (grafted US BETA.MSD) with *p expanded and a buffer as long as the line; the original turns every bare p into the name and has a 144-byte stack buffer (src/game/overrides/event_text.cpp)
unit_msg_build: English Fusion Shop lines (grafted US UNIT0n.MSD) kept host-side with *h names expanded; the original drops ASCII (src/game/overrides/event_text.cpp)
unit_msg_reveal: typewriter for those English lines, drawn through the text renderer
deck shuffle of player a0: skipped (only the pending count cleared) while the trainer's 'deck in order' is on for that player (src/game/overrides/battle.cpp)
fusion_roll (Fusion Shop, second card picked): re-rolled while the trainer's fusion toggles ask for a mutation / a Digi-Jewel (src/game/overrides/fusion.cpp)
battle DP of player a0: returns the value a battle hotkey locked (src/game/overrides/battle.cpp), else the original
text draw: ASCII strings take the US-renderer port, SJIS falls back to the JP original
text measure: same ASCII/SJIS dispatch as draw
condensed draw: ASCII takes the normal US port, SJIS the JP condensed original
condensed measure: same dispatch as condensed draw

dialog_setup: a choice box with no text and the OPENSEG labels miru/minai (the new-game 'see the explanation?' choices) gets the default labels hai/iie, drawn Yes/No; the catalog's one translation of miru/minai is the battle option's On/Off (src/game/overrides/dialog_labels.cpp)
text icon: level badges 16-19 (JP III, A, IV, kan) drawn as the US R/A/C/U badges from the private sheet when the English assets are loaded (src/game/overrides/level_badges.cpp)
mini font draw (8x7; the grey wrapper 80028898 calls it): catalog translation, English drawn with proportional ink widths, JP to the original (src/game/overrides/mini_text.cpp)
sjis_to_mini: ASCII card names copied through (the original drops every ASCII letter), SJIS to the original

bigname_load (VS-screen big name, task): ASCII names drawn with the US 16x32 font from en_bigfont.bin (the JP loader asks for FONT\%04X.tim files that do not exist); Shift-JIS to the original (src/game/overrides/bigname.cpp)
vs_names_load (VS screen, task): re-implemented so an ASCII name gets 16 px per character (the JP width (strlen/2)*32 drops odd letters); everything else as the original

vs_record_draw (VS / result screen record strip): the original, then, when the strip in VRAM is the US one without the kanji (swap_us_images.py), the words for battles / wins / losses drawn through the text call (src/game/overrides/vs_record.cpp)
player name entry, per frame: the ABC/123 page first (row table rotated, tab labels aliased; src/game/overrides/name_entry.cpp)
deck name entry, per frame: the ABC/123 page first (as the player name entry)
WORD INPUT keyword entry, per frame: the ABC/123 page first (as the player name entry)
WORD INPUT keyword pad input: as the player name entry (half-width letters, so the US keywords fit; a kana dash types '-')
WORD INPUT keyword box (window callback): as the player name box
msd_vm_step (the script VM): the original, then the port's city host command 0x0A cmd 0x40 (Custom Battle's screen; src/game/overrides/custom_battle.cpp)
city_main_task: back from a battle started in the city scene itself (Custom Battle: scene 0xFF) a plain entry, not an arena talk scene with portraits (custom_battle.cpp)
city_menu_probe_item (runs the script ahead from each menu pick to its host command, to grey out places): the original, with the port's host commands only looked at, not run (custom_battle.cpp)
city_menu_draw: the original, then the Custom Battle label on the blank button (item 10)

keyword_check (Wizardmon's spell): the original, then a keyword it did not match is matched as text (JP or US keywords), and CARDnnn / DIGIPARTnnn give a missing card / Digi-Part (src/game/overrides/keyword.cpp)
player name entry pad input: the original, then circle/triangle/cross done on bytes so the ABC page types half-width letters (12 per name; src/game/overrides/name_entry.cpp)
deck name entry pad input: as the player name entry
player name box (window callback): the name drawn verbatim, L1/R1 and the underline by whole 1-/2-byte characters
deck name box (window callback, name + Deck label): as the player name box

card_db_load: the original (CARD2.CDD as it is, so the heap and game_data stay put), then the database with the new cards' records after the 191 Digimon rebuilt in port RAM and the record bases pointed there (src/game/cards/cards.cpp)
card_record_get(n): the new cards (301 on) are Digimon records after the 191 (CARD2.CDD extended), not Digivolve records past the end (src/game/cards/cards.cpp)
card_specialty_icon(n): a new card's specialty from its record (the original says Digivolve above 292)
card_level_icon(n): a new card's level from its record
card_from_kind_index(kind, index): Digimon index 191 + k is new card 301 + k
deck_entry_set(entry, n): new card 301 + k stored as Digimon index 191 + k

deck_store (Deck Edit saving a deck): the original rebuilds each entry's card number from kind + index (a Digimon's number = its index); the new cards' numbers put back (index 191 would read as card 191, Golden Banana; src/game/cards/cards.cpp)
the battle's card picture cache slot, chosen by a card number made from kind + index inline: native, with card_from_kind_index
digimon_record_by_model(model): searches the new cards' records too (the original stops at 191)
card_copy_serial(player, card, copy): none for a new card (its serials would land in the city flags; only the trade reads them)

battle_rewards_pick(player, class): native, the same pools and rand() calls over every card including the new ones (the original reads numbers above 292 as Digivolve records and sizes its lists for 301; src/game/cards/cards.cpp)
best damage per Digimon index (game_data +0xD0C, 191 entries): skipped for a new card, whose index is past the array
battle_ko_check: KOs scored / taken per Digimon index (191 entries): the original, with the bytes a new card's index lands on put back

tables_build (Card Menu / Deck Edit record pointers by card number, 801F7178 / 801F7638): the original, then the new cards' entries (the tables have 3 spare words each; src/game/cards/card_screens.cpp)
Card Menu task: the card list's row count (static data 801F5CE4, 301) raised to the new limit first
Deck Edit init: as the Card Menu task (the shared card list's row count)
pages_build (the 8 type pages): the original, then each new card on its specialty's page (40 per page)
Card Menu totals: the original (its range split would count new cards as Digivolve), then the new cards' copies / seen added
list_icon (Deck Edit's 24x24 DECK.TIS icons): a new card draws its base card's icon (no slot above 300)
Card Menu card page: per-Digimon stats (arrays of 191 by card number) read 0 for a new card
Deck Edit card panel: as the Card Menu card page
libcd CdSearchFile: answered from the disc's root directory without reading it through the drive (the movie player looks up DIGIMON.MOV)
